brands.name: Chalets Hocking Hills
brands.story:
What makes it itself: Every single Chalets Hocking Hills property, from a one bedroom cabin to an eight guest lodge, comes with its own outdoor pool, hot tub, and fire pit. That combination, not just a hot tub alone, is the rare thing guests remember and what separates this brand from the standard single hot tub cabin nearby.

Who books and why: Couples booking the compact Legends Lane or Ravine cabins for a quiet weekend, and larger families or friend groups filling Treetop, Lakeview, or Sycamore for reunions near Hocking Hills State Park. The A-Frame collection in Logan draws repeat visitors who want that specific architectural look.

Voice: Confident and direct, matter of fact about what is included rather than gushing about woods and relaxation. Example headline: "Pool, hot tub, fire pit. Every cabin, every stay."

Avoid: Do not lead with "cozy retreat" or "nestled in nature" language that any Hocking Hills listing could claim. Do not photograph the fireplace or patio alone without showing the pool and hot tub together, since that pairing is the actual differentiator, not a bonus amenity.

brands.name: Hollyhock Suites
brands.story:
A portfolio of downtown Louisville suites and lofts, many overlooking the river or city, built for groups—from couples to 40-guest full-building buyouts. The throughline is dark, moody, well-appointed interiors paired with walkable proximity to Main Street's distilleries, restaurants, and bars.

Who books and why: Bachelorette parties, Derby weekends, distillery-hopping groups, and multi-family gatherings that need real bedroom counts (up to 8 beds, 4 baths) without sacrificing style or a central location.

Voice: Confident, warm, locally fluent—like a friend who knows exactly which door code and which bar. Short, assured sentences. Example headline: "Steps from Main Street. Zero guesswork."

Ad card headlines: short and warm, the way our designer writes them: the kind of space and its best feature, or one warm word for its style. "Modern loft with river views", "Soaking tub & city views", "Suite by the Convention Center", "Two-story loft suite", "Coffee bar & soaking tub", "Entire building with 7 suites", "Chic suite with a soaking tub". City and river views, soaking tubs, kitchens and a location a guest knows are reliable leads, and cards may share them. Every suite is in Louisville, so the headline spends its words on the space. The facts line already carries bedrooms, baths and guests. Sentence case, "&" to join two ideas. Screens, wifi, appliances and blackout curtains are expected in every suite, so they support a card and never lead it.

brands.story:
What makes it itself: two waters, one town. Every home sits on Greers Ferry Lake or the Little Red River, most with private docks, swim coves, or fishing right off the deck. Guests remember the water at their back door, not the house.

Who books and why: multigenerational families and small groups chasing quiet, fishing trips built around a dock, and repeat guests who've found their spot and keep coming back to the same cabin or lake.

Voice: calm, specific, unhurried, like a local pointing you to the right dock. Say what's actually at the water's edge, not what's in the house. Example headline: "Wake up, walk to the dock, catch breakfast."

Avoid: generic lake talk (serene getaway, home away from home), stock pool/deck photos with no water in frame, listing amenities every rental has (WiFi, linens, AC), and any language that could describe a lake house anywhere else in the country.

homes.name: Ross Ranch and Vineyards
homes.description:
Sonoma and Napa have hundreds of wineries you can visit. Ross Ranch is one of the only ones you can actually stay at. This is a real, working vineyard and ranch, not a vineyard view backdrop, with its own estate Cabernet, resident horses, cows, chickens, and peacocks, and a working garden. Book a private tasting of the ranch's own wine, gather fresh eggs from the henhouse, and wander vine rows that are actually being farmed, then spend the rest of your stay across two full houses plus a vintage Airstream: seven bedrooms, five bathrooms, room for 14, with a heated pool, a second pool built from a repurposed shipping container overlooking the vines, a brand new pickleball court, and a Peloton equipped gym. It's wine country the way it actually works, with the resort amenities layered on top.

This home is proudly managed by LegacyRnR, your local Wine Country hospitality experts. We're here to make your stay effortless and unforgettable—from arrival to check-out.

Need transportation for wine tasting or group outings?
We offer two private, comfortable options:

11-Passenger Wine Tour Van – Perfect for group tastings, birthday trips, or bachelorette weekends.
6-Passenger Cadillac Escalade – Ride in style for intimate wine tours, airport pickups, or dinner reservations.

When you book with LegacyRnR, you’re not just booking a home—you’re booking your entire Wine Country experience, curated by locals who care.

🍇 A Working Vineyard You Actually Get to Stay At

This is the part that makes Ross Ranch different from almost every other wine country rental: it's a working vineyard and ranch, actively farmed, not a property that happens to have a nice view of someone else's vines. The estate produces its own Cabernet, and private tastings of it can be arranged right on the property for your group, paired, if you'd like, with a farm to table chef's dinner cooked with vegetables and herbs pulled from the ranch's own garden.

Beyond the vines, it's a real working ranch: horses and cows graze the pasture, chickens and peacocks roam freely, and gathering the morning's fresh eggs has become one of the details past guests mention most. Kids and adults alike end up spending as much time with the animals and the garden as they do at the pool.

🏡 House Highlights
🍇 A working vineyard with its own estate wine. Private tastings can be arranged on site.
🍽️ Farm to table chef's dinners available on request, using produce from the ranch's own garden
🐴 A real working ranch: resident horses, cows, chickens, and peacocks; fresh eggs most mornings
🏠 Two full houses plus a vintage Airstream: Casa One and Casa Two, seven bedrooms and five bathrooms combined, two full kitchens, both houses with their own living and dining spaces
🏊 Two pools, two moods: a heated pool at the event barn for group time, plus a private shipping container pool at Casa Two with unobstructed vineyard and hillside views
🏓 Brand new pickleball court
🏋️ Standalone gym: two Peloton bikes, free weights, a rowing machine, and a smart TV
🔥 Fire pit and BBQ grill for evenings outdoors
🚐 Private wine country transportation: an 11 passenger van and a 6 passenger Cadillac Escalade available through your host for tastings, airport runs, or dinner reservations
🅿️ Ample free parking on site

Ross Ranch & Vineyards spans two distinct houses plus a vintage Airstream across a working ranch and vineyard property, giving your group full run of seven bedrooms and five bathrooms without ever feeling like you're sharing a hallway with strangers. Each house has its own fully equipped kitchen, spacious living and dining areas, and dedicated laundry.

Casa One sleeps in a Queen primary suite plus two additional bedrooms (a Full and a Queen). Casa Two offers a King primary suite plus two additional Queen bedrooms. The Airstream adds a seventh bedroom with a double bed, a fun, private spot for two, with its own electricity, a fridge, a small dining table with a bench, and a sink. It doesn't have its own bathroom or kitchen hookup, so those two guests will use one of the five bathrooms in the main houses. Between the two houses and the Airstream, you've got flexible sleeping for families, couples, and larger groups traveling together without compromise.

Outside is where the property really sets itself apart. The vines are actively farmed, and the ranch's own estate Cabernet can be poured for your group at a private tasting arranged right here, not at a tasting room down the road. The garden supplies vegetables and herbs for a farm to table chef's dinner if you'd like one, and the resident animals (horses, cows, chickens, peacocks) are part of daily life on the property, not decoration. Then there's the resort side of things: a heated pool right next to the event barn for group time, a second, more secluded pool at Casa Two built from a repurposed shipping container with sweeping vineyard and hillside views, a brand new pickleball court, and a fully equipped standalone gym (two Peloton bikes, free weights, rowing machine, smart TV).

The Airstream has electricity, a fridge, a small dining table with a bench, and a sink, but no private bathroom or kitchen. Guests staying there will use one of the five bathrooms and either kitchen in the main houses.
homes.locationDescription: Nestled in the heart of the world famous Napa Valley, Ross Ranch and Vineyards offers a serene escape in the scenic hills of Calistoga. While our property serves as a private sanctuary, you are perfectly positioned to explore the best of California wine country. You will find yourself just a short ten to fifteen minute drive from the charming downtown area of Calistoga, where you can indulge in exquisite farm to table dining, boutique shopping, and the famous mineral hot springs. For outdoor enthusiasts, the area is a paradise for cycling and hiking, with breathtaking trails accessible within a fifteen minute drive. Whether you are looking to visit world class vineyards for wine tasting or prefer a scenic drive through the rolling hills, our location provides the perfect balance of seclusion and convenience for your group getaway.
